headline_findings: THE 'MYOPIC HEURISTICS' GAP IS CLOSED, AND THE PAPER IS ABOUT EXACTLY THIS PROJECT'S PROBLEM. Chen, Prakash, Lima De Azevedo & Ben-Akiva, TR-C 119:102650 (2020): 'Existing calibration approaches are myopic heuristics in the sense that they do not consider the fundamental inter-dependencies among choice-models and do not have a systematic way to adjust model parameters.' Their target set is this project's target set, verbatim: 'activity shares, mode shares, time-dependent & mode-specific OD flows, and time-dependent & mode-specific sensor counts.'

THE PROFESSION HAS PUT IN WRITING THAT THE THING THIS PROJECT IS TRYING TO DO IS NOT NORMALLY ATTEMPTED. WFRC/RSG ActivitySim Implementation Framework, section 4.4, verbatim: 'It is typically the case that not all calibration and validation targets can be achieved simultaneously. Therefore, model calibration and validation requires judgement on when the models are reasonably calibrated and validated and ready for applications.' The state of practice substitutes professional judgement for the goal.

BUT THE ARCHITECTURE THAT DOES SOLVE IT EXISTS, IT IS A MAXIMUM AND NOT A SUM, AND IT NOW HAS A WORKED POLICY-ABM APPLICATION. O'Gara et al. (arXiv 2501.00616) on Covasim: 'since the system at hand contains multiple outputs, we use the maximum implausibility measure across Q outputs I_M(theta) = max_q I_q(theta).' A parameter set survives only if EVERY output is plausible - 'all N targets inside their bands' as the object being solved. Four waves, ~50 designs x 20-25 replicates each, cutoff tightened 3.0 -> 2.5, outputs ADDED wave by wave, NROY volume 7.23% -> 5.58% -> 0.82%, >99% of space ruled out, then ABC over the survivor. Model discrepancy is an EXPLICIT term in the denominator, and an empty NROY region is a formal verdict that 'this would require revisiting both the model itself and the model discrepancy'.

WHY CONVERGENCE MADE THIS PROJECT'S FIT WORSE HAS A PUBLISHED DIAGNOSIS, IN MATSim'S OWN BOOK, AND IT IS NOT A TASTE PARAMETER. Floetteroed & Kickhoefer, ch. 49, verbatim: 'When a policy study's synthetic choice sets are very different from the alternatives considered in the real world, it is unlikely that the simulation will display correct aggregated quantities or useful sensitivities for policy measures.' The board records final PT choice-set coverage at 25.78%. The same chapter pairs disabling innovation with SCORE MSA - 'fractionOfIterationsToDisableInnovation' AND 'fractionOfIterationsToStartScoreMSA' - and this project disabled innovation alone, then watched car snap +2.211 pp and the average plan score fall from 19.2049 to 14.5679. And from the developers' own thread (tduberne, matsim-code-examples #25): 'it is quite typical to have the executed score pretty close to the worst score, for those simulation with mode choice enabled', and 'Yes, mode shares do stabilize as well, only slower' than scores - so a flat score curve is not evidence that shares have settled.

THE AGENCY ASC RULE THIS PROJECT IMPLEMENTED IS THE PUBLISHED STANDARD, INSIDE A CYCLIC PROTOCOL THIS PROJECT DOES NOT HAVE. WFRC/RSG, verbatim: 'New ASC = Old ASC + ln(Target Proportion / Model Proportion)', and 'several models must be calibrated in tandem... calibration of ActivitySim should be performed in an iterative, cyclic fashion... Each cycle of re-calibration achieves increasingly precise matches between the modeled outcomes and the targets as the influences between model components reached an equilibrium.' The same document maps residuals to MECHANISMS: screenline count errors indicate 'the need to improve the quality of the input network or land-use data, modify the skimming process, or introduce an adjustment in destination choice', and a boarding-rate error indicates 'the need for a lower or higher transfer penalty in mode choice'.

SOMEBODY HAS PAID FOR A LARGE SIMULTANEOUS MULTI-TARGET CALIBRATION AND PUBLISHED THE PRICE. Tallinn / SimMobility MT Preday (Agriesti et al.): 477 behavioural parameters - 'prior literature had only tackled up to 98' - against a custom objective of THREE equally weighted components (OD matrix, mode-share distribution, employment coverage), by Bayesian optimisation over a Random-Forest surrogate; up to 500 iterations, satisfactory at 150-182, '6-8 hours on a laptop' per full-population run; final 'error for the overall number of trips is equal to 4% and the average error in the OD matrix is 15.92 vehicles per day'. Order 1,000 machine hours. This project's own coordinate-descent budget line prices ~18 arms and ~140 machine hours and has never been run to completion.

THE COUNTS DEFICIT IS NOT EXPLAINED BY THE SAMPLE, AND THE LITERATURE POINTS SOMEWHERE ELSE. TF Resource, verbatim: 'Auxiliary demand refers to trips that are not represented in the activity-based model system, such as truck trips, visitor trips, internal-external and external-external trips, and special generator trips.' Meanwhile the MUM 2025 downsampling study (Mersini & Ziemke, TU Berlin, on the Lausitz 100% scenario) concludes that average statistics 'become unreliable when sampling below 10%' - placing this project's 25% inside the reliable band. No source read this pass attributes a ~99% volume deficit to sample scaling.

THE ACCEPTANCE-BAR VACUUM IS WIDER THAN THE LIBRARY RECORDED. Last pass established 'There are no applicable criteria guidelines for checks of mode choice.' This pass read TF Resource's Amount-Of-Travel validation page and found the same for the count side: 'There are no specific criteria guidelines associated with the trip generation checks described above', and for external models, truck models and special generators, 'There are no applicable criteria guidelines.' The only numeric ranges on that page are 0.90-1.10 for regionwide productions to attractions and 1.20-1.55 home-based work attractions per employee. So neither the 10% mode band NOR any count tolerance this project might adopt has a published criterion behind it.

related_methods_study.title: Scaling traffic flow properties of MATSim to correctly cooperate for population downsampling
related_methods_study.authors: Theresa-Maria Mersini and Theresa Ziemke, Transport Systems Planning and Transport Telematics, TU Berlin
related_methods_study.venue: MATSim User Meeting 2025, paper 30 (preliminary results; the full study is not yet published)
related_methods_study.why_it_matters_here: The ONLY systematic study read in seven passes of what a sample fraction does to a MATSim result, and it is run on a project row this library already holds. It uses the Lausitz scenario as a rare full-scale (100%) reference - 470k links, 260k nodes, 1,195,422 agents, filtered to a 305,200-agent car-leg benchmark - and simulates the shares 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0 at 500 iterations each, with ten differently sampled populations per small share and ten seeds on two of them. VERBATIM CONCLUSION: 'Preliminary comparisons of scores and travel times suggest that even average statistics (such as score and travel time) become unreliable when sampling below 10%.' It also finds stuck-time violations scale badly: about 40k in the 100% sample ('almost 1/8 of the agents getting stuck once per day'), three times as many at 1%, and 'more than four and a half times as many' at 1% with equal flow/storage scaling. On alpha it is agnostic so far: 'adjusting the scaling of storage capacity may not be necessary', but only because travel times hide the stuck-time damage.
related_methods_study.bearing_on_our_row: This project runs at 25% by standing directive, which this study places comfortably inside the reliable band and ABOVE the 10% line where its own averages break down. It does NOT explain a counts deficit: nothing in it says a correctly scaled sample loses link volume. So the -98.75% median at our 30 count stations is NOT diagnosed by sample scaling on the evidence read this pass.

It ran up to 500 iterations, reaching satisfactory performance at iteration 150-182, with each individual run taking '6-8 hours on a laptop' for the full population. It also publishes a SEPARATE architecture for the demand/supply equilibrium: an equilibrium-seeking search that measures 'the difference in traffic patterns between consecutive iterations' and needs 15 iterations to bring it under 10%.

platforms.calibration_tooling: Three named routes, all read this pass: (1) matsim.calibration in matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools - an ASCCalibrator driving an Optuna study, whose update is literally log(z_i) - log(m_i) - (log(z_0) - log(m_0)), i.e. the classic ASC fixed-point loop normalised on a fixed reference mode, with a pluggable learning-rate scheduler and a TerminationCondition dataclass whose check_termination carries "# TODO: not used yet"; (2) Cadyts, a Bayesian count calibration that adjusts NO parameter and instead adds a utility bonus so agents select the plans matching observed counts; (3) opdyts (Flotterod, TR-B 2017), which approximates point equilibria of the mobsim/scoring/replanning loop, with a Berlin mode-constant example. gaps.gap: NEW - is a four-step model's per-mode transit validation the same rung, or a different ladder?
gaps.detail: This pass found the top rung reached - but by a TRIP-BASED FOUR-STEP model, not by an agent-based one. WFTDM (Utah) reports six transit modes separately with every reported mode inside 10% and most inside 5%. It is excluded from the survey because it has no agents, which is correct under the qualification rule, but it exposes a real question the ladder does not currently ask: the top rung may be empty among AGENT-BASED models not because it is hard to reach but because agent-based projects do not report at that granularity, while the agency four-step world routinely does. Answering it changes what 'nobody else attempts this' means in the report.
gaps.query: SEMCOG / MWCOG Gen3 / SANDAG ABM3 / CMAP 'Model Calibration and Validation Report' PDFs specifically - look for a boardings-by-mode table with an observed column and a percent-difference column. Try semcog.org and mwcog.org direct PDF paths; CMAP's own PDF is recorded as an image-only scan.
gaps.closed_note: PARTLY CLOSED, and the answer moves the report's claim in an honest direction. The WFRC/RSG ActivitySim Implementation Framework (21 Feb 2025), read in full this pass, lists under 'Validation summaries' in its Table 29: 'Traffic counts and VMT by volume group', 'Traffic counts and VMT by facility type', 'Traffic counts by screenline', 'Transit boardings by operator', 'TRANSIT BOARDINGS BY TRANSIT MODE', and 'Number of transfers'. So per-transit-mode boardings IS a standard planned validation summary for an agency ACTIVITY-BASED model, not only for the four-step world. The top rung of this survey is therefore empty not because agent-based projects cannot report at that granularity, but because the PUBLISHED artefacts read in seven passes do not carry the per-mode deviation TABLE WITH BANDS. STILL OPEN: an actual agency ABM validation report showing per-transit-mode boardings with deviations, which is what would settle whether the rung is reached in practice or only planned.

gaps.gap: NEW - nobody has published an account of an agent-based model matching mode SHARES while missing absolute link VOLUMES by two orders of magnitude
gaps.detail: This was the pass's second-priority lane and it produced a STRUCTURAL explanation but no matching case. What was found: (a) 'auxiliary demand' - trucks, visitors, internal-external, external-external and special-generator trips are outside a resident ABM by construction and must be supplied separately (TF Resource, verbatim, written into calibration_methods); (b) TF Resource states there are no numeric acceptance criteria for count validation, external models, truck models or special generators; (c) the MUM 2025 downsampling study (Mersini & Ziemke, TU Berlin) finds average statistics 'become unreliable when sampling below 10%', which places this project's 25% INSIDE the reliable band and therefore does NOT explain the deficit. WHAT IS MISSING is a published case with a number: an ABM whose mode shares were acceptable and whose counts were out by ~90-99%, with the cause diagnosed. Four differently phrased searches (cordon/through traffic; MATSim link volumes; missing demand components; capacity scaling) returned no such case. It may simply not be publishable - a model that far out on counts does not get written up.

calibration_method.family: coordinate descent over registry-declared sweeps (unchanged, never run to completion) PLUS, NEW AT THIS HEAD AND NEVER RUN, an implemented ASC log-ratio fixed point - src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py. Read from the source at HEAD 781cf41, not searched.
calibration_method.what_the_source_says: src/calibrate/calibrate.py:508-533 runs coordinate descent: per round, per free parameter, per grid point across that parameter's registry sweep, a FULL MATSim run -> extract_metrics -> fit -> a weighted scalar objective over declared _fit.json components, keeping a point only if it is feasible against the C4 occupancy and trip-length constraints; the round stops when the improvement falls below delta. The search space is DERIVED FROM THE REGISTRY, not listed in the script: a field is free only if it is source=assumed, carries a scalar sweep and is not held_fixed. The six mode constants are held_fixed under DECISIONS.md 8.5 and are therefore unreachable from the loop by construction - so this project has NO log(target/modelled) ASC loop of any kind. The one constant that is solved, asc_car_passenger, is solved in a separate module (solve_asc_ride.py:101-121) by SECANT INTERPOLATION ON log(ride_per_car) against the observed passenger:driver ratio, and is reported as a CONSTRAINT, not an estimate. The loop refuses to fit more parameters than the objective identifies (four independent numbers) and cannot read a holdout row by construction.
calibration_method.objective_evaluations: coordinate descent: calibrate.py:433 computes the budget as sum(len(grid(p, points_per_param)) for p in free) * max_rounds FULL MATSim runs; at 25% an arm reaching iteration 100 cost 7.66 h wall, so a 3-point 3-parameter 2-round search is ~18 arms and ~140 machine hours. THE LOOP HAS NEVER BEEN RUN TO COMPLETION. The ASC fixed point is far cheaper by design - TWO arms settle the contraction question - and is the only one of the two that has an evaluation count small enough to state in advance. Neither has been executed.
calibration_method.asc_fixed_point_new_this_pass: src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py EXISTS and PROPOSES ONLY; it has NEVER BEEN RUN. It applies delta_i = damping * [ ln(target_i/modelled_i) - ln(target_ref/modelled_ref) ] against car as reference - the same object as the Berry (1994) share inversion and the same expression matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools computes verbatim, with the damping declared on CAL.asc.damping. THREE DESIGN CHOICES ARE UNUSUAL AND WORTH RECORDING: (1) THE TEST IS THE CONTRACTION, NOT THE SHARES - two damped rounds are compared mode by mode, and if |delta| shrinks the residual is a taste that constants will close, while if it does not shrink the deficit is STRUCTURAL and no constant will ever close it. That is a cheap, decisive, published-in-spirit answer to the 'constant or mechanism' question that the agency protocol answers only by ordering. (2) It CANNOT REACH A FROZEN CONSTANT: it reads held_fixed from the registry and refuses, structurally, the way the holdout guard refuses. (3) On heavy rail and light rail the step is marked basis_is_boardings and reported as a PROXY, because the logit inversion is exact only for shares of a common total. ROUND 1 IS PROPOSED OFF THE F31 GATE AND NOT APPLIED: bike -0.5121, bus -0.2301, ferry +0.6713, light rail +0.4143.
calibration_method.read_against_the_field_this_pass: Two published methods now bracket this project's loop and both were read this pass. (1) Chen, Prakash, Lima de Azevedo & Ben-Akiva (2020, TR-C 119:102650) names this project's coordinate descent for what it is: 'myopic heuristics in the sense that they do not consider the fundamental inter-dependencies among choice-models and do not have a systematic way to adjust model parameters' - and their non-myopic alternative calibrates precisely this project's target set at once (activity shares, mode shares, mode-specific OD flows, mode-specific sensor counts). (2) The WFRC/RSG ActivitySim framework publishes `New ASC = Old ASC + ln(Target Proportion / Model Proportion)` verbatim - the exact expression in asc_fixed_point.py - inside a CYCLIC protocol over model components, and states plainly that 'It is typically the case that not all calibration and validation targets can be achieved simultaneously.'

calibration_methods.method: ASC fixed-point loop (the classic log-ratio update)
calibration_methods.family: fixed-point / heuristic root-find, no optimiser
calibration_methods.implemented_in: matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools, matsim.calibration.ASCCalibrator, driving an Optuna study
calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: the alternative-specific constant of each mode, all modes at once, normalised on a fixed reference mode
calibration_methods.update_rule: calc_asc_update returns, verbatim from base.py: math.log(z_i) - math.log(m_i) - (math.log(z_0) - math.log(m_0)) - where z is the observed share, m the simulated share, and subscript 0 the fixed reference mode. A learning rate is applied outside this call.
calibration_methods.objective_evaluations: one full MATSim run per outer trial; no count is documented
calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: DECLARED BUT NOT IMPLEMENTED: a TerminationCondition dataclass carries abs_error and rel_error, and check_termination carries the comment "# TODO: not used yet". No default learning-rate scheduler is provided; subclasses must supply one.
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: This is the reference answer to 'how does a twelve-mode model reach equilibrium across simultaneous share targets' in the MATSim world - and the leading implementation of it has no working stopping rule.

calibration_methods.method: Cadyts - Bayesian demand calibration
calibration_methods.family: Bayesian updating of the plan-choice distribution; NOT parameter search
calibration_methods.implemented_in: MATSim (CadytsModule contrib) and SUMO (SUMO-Cadyts); Flotterod, Bierlaire, Nagel
calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: nothing in the utility function. "Cadyts does not adjust any parameters when it calibrates MATSim. Instead, it tries to select and execute the optimal daily plans in each agent's memory" - it adds "an extra positive utility" to the plans whose simulated counts match the observed ones.
calibration_methods.update_rule: "In a Bayesian framework, the simulation system alone provides a complete behavioral prior, which then is updated based on the traffic counts." Agent n draws plan i from a choice distribution P_n(i); the counts reweight that distribution.
calibration_methods.objective_evaluations: none as such - the correction runs INSIDE the simulation loop, not as an outer loop of full runs
calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: unknown from the sources read
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: The one architecture in the survey that attains a target WITHOUT an outer loop of full simulation runs. It is a counts method, not a mode-share method, but the mechanism - bias the plan selection, leave the parameters alone - is the structural alternative to everything else in this list.

calibration_methods.method: opdyts - approximation of point equilibria
calibration_methods.family: simulation-based optimisation with search acceleration, exploiting the mobsim/scoring/replanning fixed point
calibration_methods.implemented_in: gunnarfloetteroed/java; a MATSim Berlin example calibrates mode-specific constants to overall mode shares
calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: any decision variable of the simulation, mode constants included
calibration_methods.update_rule: "approximately solves general simulation-based optimization problems subject to transport simulation constraints"; the heuristic "approximates point equilibria, i.e. reproducible 'relaxed' states with minimal randomness in simulation setups that comprise the iterative 'mobsim/scoring/replanning' logic of MATSim" (Transportation Research Part B, 2017)
calibration_methods.objective_evaluations: unknown - the point of the method is that it does not need a converged run per evaluation, but no count was read this pass
calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: unknown
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: It is the only method read that treats the equilibrium itself as the object - it does not wait for a relaxed run before scoring a candidate, which is exactly the cost that makes our own outer loop unaffordable.

calibration_methods.method: boptx / octras - derivative-free optimiser suites for transport simulation
calibration_methods.family: evolutionary (CMA-ES, xNES) and stochastic gradient approximation (FDSA, SPSA), plus opdyts and all of scipy.optimize
calibration_methods.implemented_in: sebhoerl/boptx (successor) and sebhoerl/octras; drive eqasim/MATSim (Berlin, Corsica) and SUMO (Monaco)

calibration_methods.method: Staged / stepwise calibration, with mode constants as A LAST RESORT (the agency protocol)
calibration_methods.family: sequential protocol, not an optimiser - the published answer to 'constant or mechanism?'

calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: each model component in turn, earliest first: inputs (socioeconomic data, interchange travel times), then trip generation, then distribution, then mode choice - 'As each model is calibrated, the results are passed as input to the subsequent step in the modeling process. In this way, the impacts of error propagation are reduced throughout the modeling process.'
calibration_methods.update_rule: THE RULE THIS PROJECT HAS BEEN LOOKING FOR, and it is published verbatim: 'simple adjustments to modal constants estimated using weighted samples should be considered "a last resort" after all other possible causes for error and calibration adjustments have been considered' (TF Resource, Model Validation and Reasonableness Checking / Mode Choice). The same page states the coupling that makes multi-target mode calibration hard: 'adjustments that increase the transit shares may further decrease the nonmotorized mode shares'. It ALSO states, verbatim, that no numeric acceptance bar exists: 'There are no applicable criteria guidelines for checks of mode choice.'
calibration_methods.objective_evaluations: not applicable and not published - the protocol is a human ordering of work, not a search. No count is stated anywhere on either page.
calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: none stated; the manual's language is 'reasonably reproduce observed traffic and transit ridership'. The mode-choice page gives no tolerance at all, while the sibling pages DO give them for other components (trip length within 5%, coincidence ratio 0.7 or higher, intrazonal within 3 percentage points, P/A ratio between 0.9 and 1.1).
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: This is the strongest external corroboration the project has for its own hardest rule. DECISIONS.md 8.5 freezes the mode constants and .claude/CLAUDE.md bans compensating constants; the profession's own reference independently calls constant adjustment 'a last resort', for the same stated reason - constants stand for unmeasured comfort, reliability and safety and therefore mask structural error. It also settles that the project's 10% band is SELF-IMPOSED: the field publishes no mode-choice acceptance criterion to be measured against. And its coupling sentence is the multi-target problem in one line: moving one mode moves the others, because shares sum to one.

calibration_methods.method: History matching with an emulator - implausibility and the NROY region (waves, not a point estimate)
calibration_methods.family: set-valued calibration: it returns the set of parameter values NOT YET RULED OUT rather than one best point, and it is natively multi-target
calibration_methods.implemented_in: the agent-based-model UQ literature. THIS PASS FOUND A FULL WORKED APPLICATION TO A POLICY ABM: O'Gara, Kerr, Klein, Binois, Garnett & Hammond, 'Improving Policy-Oriented Agent-Based Modeling with History Matching: A Case Study' (arXiv 2501.00616), on COVASIM - a real, policy-used, stochastic agent-based model. Still NO application to a transport ABM.
calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: nothing directly - each WAVE fits a Gaussian process emulator to a design of simulator runs, computes an implausibility for every candidate parameter set, discards the implausible, and draws the next design only from what survives
calibration_methods.update_rule: implausibility, verbatim: 'I(x) = |z - E(f(x))| / sqrt(Var(e) + Var(d) + Var(f(x)))' - the distance between output and observation normalised by the SUM of observation error, MODEL DISCREPANCY and emulator variance. Model discrepancy is an explicit term: the method assumes from the start that the simulator is wrong somewhere and asks only to be inconsistent within that admission. CONCRETE FORM READ THIS PASS (O'Gara et al.): the data-generating process is assumed to be 'Y = g(theta) + sigma_md(theta) + sigma_o', where sigma_md 'represents the model discrepancy (accounting for any systematic deviations between simulation and reality)'. AND THE MULTI-TARGET RULE IS A MAXIMUM, NOT A SUM, VERBATIM: 'since the system at hand contains multiple outputs, we use the maximum implausibility measure across Q outputs I_M(theta) = max_{q in Q} I_q(theta).' A parameter set survives only if EVERY output is plausible - which is exactly 'all N targets inside their bands' expressed as the object being solved. The cutoff is principled rather than self-imposed: 'A common cutoff value I(theta) is 3, inspired from (Pukelsheim 1994) showing that at least 95% of any continuous unimodal distribution is contained within three standard deviations'.
calibration_methods.objective_evaluations: NOW PUBLISHED FOR A POLICY ABM (O'Gara et al.): 'a maximin Latin hypercube design of 50 model parameterizations, with 25 replicates at each design location, and at subsequent waves, used 20 replicates per design location' - so roughly 1,000-1,250 simulator runs PER WAVE, over four waves: order 4,000-5,000 runs. Covasim costs 'about 30 seconds per model run'. The emulator is what buys the search: a grid of '40 input locations for each of the four model parameters... a total of 40^4 = 2,560,000 candidate model parameterizations, which would correspond to nearly 2.5 years of computing time using the simulator, but can be evaluated via emulation in a matter of minutes'. STILL UNPUBLISHED for a transport ABM.
calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: the NROY region stops shrinking between waves, or it empties - and an EMPTY NROY region is itself the finding: no parameter value is consistent with the targets, so the model is structurally wrong. That is a formal, published test of exactly the 'taste or mechanism' question. MEASURED THIS PASS: the NROY volume fell 7.23% -> 5.58% -> 0.82% of parameter space over three reported waves, 'we removed over 99% of parameter space from consideration' after four; the implausibility cutoff was TIGHTENED as waves proceeded (3.0 -> 2.5) and OUTPUTS WERE ADDED wave by wave. The empty-NROY verdict is stated verbatim: model discrepancy 'could also be revisited under the condition where NROY space is estimated to be empty (stated differently, if we were not able to identify non-implausible model parameters, this would require revisiting both the model itself and the model discrepancy)'. The pipeline then runs ABC over the surviving region for a posterior.
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: It is the only architecture read this pass that is BUILT for many simultaneous targets and that can return 'no parameter set satisfies these twelve targets' as a result rather than as a failure. Its implausibility per output is computed INDEPENDENTLY per metric, which is the same shape as the board's twelve per-mode deviations. Cost is the barrier: it needs a design of full runs per wave, and at 25% one arm is 7.66 h wall. THE COST BARRIER IS NOW QUANTIFIED AND IT IS THE WHOLE STORY. Covasim runs in 30 seconds; this project's landed arm took 21.5 h at 25%. Four waves at O'Gara's design would be ~4,000 arms, i.e. ~86,000 machine hours - impossible. But the paper's own argument cuts the other way too: the emulator turned 2.5 years of simulator time into minutes. The transferable design for this project is a wave over CHEAP arms (1% or a short horizon) to fit an emulator, with expensive 25% arms spent only inside NROY - and the max-implausibility rule adopted in place of fit.py's weighted scalar, so that 'twelve modes inside their bands' becomes the object rather than a sum that can trade one mode off against another.

calibration_methods.method: Multi-objective formulations - weighted sum with normalisation (standard), Pareto/NSGA-II with the simulator in the loop (rare), epsilon-constraint (not found in transport calibration)
calibration_methods.family: how many targets become one number, or are refused the chance to
calibration_methods.implemented_in: weighted sum is the field default; NSGA-II has been coupled to MATSim, but for NETWORK DESIGN (searching a Pareto set of network solutions, MATSim evaluating each generation's solutions), not for parameter calibration
calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: the objective, not the parameters: 'The objective function in simulation-based calibration is often formulated as a weighted sum of squared deviations between simulated and field-observed traffic measurements - primarily link counts, speeds, and travel times', with the explicit warning that 'Performance indicators of experiments should be scaled before importing them into the optimization formula' because different measures carry different units and scales.
calibration_methods.update_rule: weighted sum: one scalar, one search, weights chosen by the modeller and rarely justified. Pareto: a front rather than a point, so no weight need be chosen - at the cost of many more evaluations. Epsilon-constraint (optimise one objective, bound the rest as inequality constraints) is the textbook way to express 'every mode inside 10%' as a constraint set rather than a sum, and NO source read this pass applies it to transport model calibration.
calibration_methods.objective_evaluations: unknown in every variant. No transport-calibration source read this pass publishes an evaluation count for a multi-objective formulation.
calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: weighted sum: the scalar stops improving (this project's coordinate descent is exactly this shape). Pareto: the front stops advancing.
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: This project's fit.py already computes a weighted scalar over declared components, so it sits in the mainstream. The gap the search exposes is that the project's ACTUAL goal - twelve constraints all satisfied at once - is a FEASIBILITY problem, and the two formulations built for it (epsilon-constraint, and history matching's NROY set) are not in use anywhere in transport calibration that this pass could find. A weighted sum can be improved by trading a good mode against a bad one; a constraint set cannot.

calibration_methods.method: THE COUNTER-FINDING - 'The Calibration Illusion in Traffic Microsimulation' (Hickert et al., 2026)
calibration_methods.family: a critique of the whole automatic-calibration literature, and the closest thing found to a published statement of what calibration actually costs
calibration_methods.implemented_in: not a method - an empirical study across five parameter categories (origin-destination, car-following, lane-change, simulation and heterogeneity parameters) on small, medium and large networks
calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: nothing - it measures what the published methods leave out
calibration_methods.update_rule: its central claim, verbatim: automatic calibration is 'largely an illusion' because 'a significant - and unquantified - amount of bespoke manual work is hidden behind these methods.' Its identifiability finding is the constant-versus-mechanism problem stated formally: 'it may not be clear whether the CFM parameters or the OD parameters need adjustment' when calibrating jointly.
calibration_methods.objective_evaluations: STILL NOT PUBLISHED, and this paper is why: the field's reported figures are the optimiser's evaluations, and the unreported figure is the human work around them. Reported comparisons on the small network: simulation-in-the-loop optimisation reached a velocity MAPE of 5.200 +/- 1.519 against a genetic algorithm's 9.588 +/- 1.866; and changing the simulation timestep by 10% 'could more than double' the mean absolute percent error.
calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: n/a. The paper's warning is that calibrating to AGGREGATE data alone under-constrains the model - 'stop-and-go waves' failed to emerge reliably even in calibrated models.
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: It corroborates the previous pass's headline (nobody publishes an evaluation count) and explains it: the count would have to include the manual work, and nobody measures that. It also warns directly against the trade this project keeps being tempted into - fitting aggregate mode shares while the mechanism underneath stays wrong - and it supplies a quantified example of a MODEL setting (the timestep, not a behavioural parameter) dominating the result, which is the same class of error as a teleported access leg or an absent crowding term.

calibration_methods.method: NON-MYOPIC simultaneous calibration of a nested-logit activity-based model SYSTEM by stochastic gradient (Chen, Prakash, Lima de Azevedo & Ben-Akiva 2020) - THE SOURCE OF THE 'MYOPIC HEURISTICS' CLAIM, FOUND AND CLOSED THIS PASS
calibration_methods.family: simulation-based optimisation with an APPROXIMATE ANALYTICAL GRADIENT derived from the model system's own nested-logit structure, evaluated on mini-batches of the population
calibration_methods.implemented_in: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies 119 (Aug 2020), 102650, doi 10.1016/j.trc.2020.102650. Siyu Chen, A. Arun Prakash, Carlos Lima De Azevedo, Moshe Ben-Akiva (the SimMobility/DynaMIT lineage; the paper does not name the city of its 'real-world application').
calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: the parameters of the estimated nested-logit activity-based model system - not one component's constants, the whole coupled system at once
calibration_methods.update_rule: VERBATIM, and it is the exact indictment this library recorded unsourced on 9 September: 'Existing calibration approaches are myopic heuristics in the sense that they do not consider the fundamental inter-dependencies among choice-models and do not have a systematic way to adjust model parameters. Also, other purely simulation-based approaches do not perform well in large-scale applications.' The remedy, verbatim: 'We formulate the calibration problem as a simulation-based optimization problem and propose a stochastic gradient-based solution procedure to solve it. The solution procedure relies on microsimulation to calculate expectations of the aggregate statistics of interest to the calibration problem. Additionally, we derive approximate analytical expressions for the gradient of the objective function - that are evaluated through microsimulation on mini-batches of the population. The proposed solution procedure is sensitive to the fundamental structure of the activity-based model-system and is non-myopic in considering the dependencies across its model components.'
calibration_methods.the_targets: THE CLOSEST PUBLISHED MATCH TO THIS PROJECT'S QUESTION. Verbatim: 'we focus on utility-maximizing nested logit activity-based model-systems and calibrating aggregate statistics such as activity shares, mode shares, time-dependent & mode-specific OD flows, and time-dependent & mode-specific sensor counts.' That is mode shares AND link/sensor counts AND OD flows, in one objective, by design.
calibration_methods.objective_evaluations: unknown - the abstract claims the procedure 'outperforms other state-of-the-art purely simulation-based optimization approaches in terms of computational efficiency, stability, and convergence' but states no run count; the full text was not reached (the accepted manuscript sits behind sciencedirect.com/science/article/am/pii/S0968090X20305659, a route this library records as 403).
calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: not stated in the abstract. The paper explicitly warns the landscape is hostile: 'The formulated optimization problem is non-convex, highly nonlinear, and potentially has multiple-minima.'
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: It answers the question this project has been asking from the inside. The reason a mode-by-mode constant update cannot close twelve targets is NOT that the arithmetic is wrong - it is that each component's parameter moves every other component's output, and a per-mode heuristic has no representation of that coupling. This project's src/calibrate/calibrate.py coordinate descent is, in this paper's terms, exactly a myopic heuristic: it moves one registry field at a time and re-reads a scalar. The paper's alternative needs the model system's ANALYTICAL structure to derive a gradient - which MATSim's co-evolutionary loop does not expose, so the method is not directly portable. The transferable part is the DIAGNOSIS and the target set, not the algorithm.

calibration_methods.implemented_in: arXiv 2302.03480, IEEE Open Journal of Intelligent Transportation Systems. Serio Agriesti, Vladimir Kuzmanovski, Jaakko Hollmen, Claudio Roncoli, Bat-hen Nahmias-Biran.
calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: 477 behavioural parameters across the nested-logit utility functions of a full activity-based model system - 'prior literature had only tackled up to 98 parameters'

A weighted sum, but a declared and equal one, over structurally different target families.
calibration_methods.objective_evaluations: PUBLISHED AND USABLE: up to 500 iterations, with satisfactory performance reached around iteration 150-182; 'Each individual run took 6-8 hours on a laptop (Intel core i5 - 1.60 GHz x 8)' for a full-population simulation. So the demonstrated price of a 477-parameter three-target automatic calibration is order 150 runs x 7 h ~ 1,000 machine hours.
calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: no improvement over the surrogate within the iteration budget; final reported fit 'The error for the overall number of trips is equal to 4% and the average error in the OD matrix is 15.92 vehicles per day.'
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: The single most useful cost benchmark this library holds. This project's calibrate.py budget line (calibrate.py:433) prices a 3-point 3-parameter 2-round coordinate descent at ~18 arms and ~140 machine hours and it has NEVER been run to completion. Tallinn paid ~1,000 machine hours and got 477 parameters against three simultaneous targets. The gap is not compute, it is the search: a surrogate lets a wave of runs inform the whole space, where coordinate descent spends each run on one axis. It also records, verbatim, why the manual route is not an option at this size: manual calibration of hundreds of parameters 'would hardly be performed by hand', and 'a unified calibration approach... able to include hundreds of parameters, is still needed.'

calibration_methods.method: CYCLIC component-by-component ASC calibration driven to an internal equilibrium - the ActivitySim agency protocol, written down (WFRC / RSG, Activity-Based Model Implementation Framework, 21 Feb 2025)
calibration_methods.family: sequential coordinate-wise fixed point over MODEL COMPONENTS, repeated in cycles until the components stop moving one another; a human judges the stop
calibration_methods.implemented_in: Wasatch Front Regional Council 'Activity-Based Model Implementation Framework' (ActivitySim; Wasatch Front region, Utah), sections 4.3 Model Calibration and 4.4 Model Validation, read in full this pass.
calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: the alternative-specific constants (and other limited parameters) of each MNL/NL component in turn - auto ownership, work-from-home, location choice, daily activity pattern, tour frequency, tour mode, stop frequency, trip mode, and the rest of Table 29
calibration_methods.update_rule: THE LOG-RATIO FIXED POINT, PUBLISHED AS AGENCY PRACTICE AND VERBATIM: 'New ASC = Old ASC + ln(Target Proportion / Model Proportion)'. Steps, verbatim: '2. The ActivitySim specification and coefficients file for the appropriate model is updated with the new coefficients. 3. The model is run with the updated coefficients. 4. If the model reasonably matches the observed data, stop; otherwise, go to step 1.' This is character-for-character the update in this project's src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py, which has still never been run.
calibration_methods.the_coupling_rule: THE PART THAT ANSWERS THIS PASS'S QUESTION, VERBATIM: 'Each of the series of models in ActivitySim influences other models in the system. Not only are long-term decisions made in early models used to determine short-term decisions in later models, but the parameters in the later short-term decisions also influence long-term decisions through the inclusion of the maximum expected utility, or logsum, from key short-term models as an explanatory variable in some of the long-term models. Therefore, several models must be calibrated in tandem. Because of these influences between model components, calibration of ActivitySim should be performed in an iterative, cyclic fashion. The calibration team progresses through each step in the model system in order, adjusting or re-estimating model parameters until the aggregate outcomes from the model matches the targets. Each cycle of re-calibration achieves increasingly precise matches between the modeled outcomes and the targets as the influences between model components reached an equilibrium.'
calibration_methods.the_admission: AND THE PROFESSION'S OWN VERDICT ON WHETHER ALL TARGETS CAN BE MET AT ONCE, VERBATIM AND UNQUALIFIED: 'It is typically the case that not all calibration and validation targets can be achieved simultaneously. Therefore, model calibration and validation requires judgement on when the models are reasonably calibrated and validated and ready for applications.' This is the clearest published statement found in seven passes that the state of practice does NOT solve 'all N targets inside their bands' - it declares the goal unattainable in general and substitutes professional judgement.
calibration_methods.the_residual_diagnosis_table: ALSO PUBLISHED HERE, and directly reusable, VERBATIM: 'comparison of assignment results to traffic counts on screenlines might indicate the need to improve the quality of the input network or land-use data, modify the skimming process, or introduce an adjustment in destination choice. A boarding rate comparison in transit assignment might indicate the need for a lower or higher transfer penalty in mode choice.' That maps a residual to a MECHANISM rather than to a constant - the question this project's ASC contraction test was built to answer.
calibration_methods.objective_evaluations: unstated as a number: one full model run per cycle per component adjusted, cycles 'until the aggregate outcomes from the model matches the targets'.
calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: 'If the model reasonably matches the observed data, stop' - a human, explicitly. No numeric acceptance band is given for any calibration summary.
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: Three things this project can use immediately. (1) Its ASC fixed point is not an idiosyncrasy; it is the agency standard, written out. (2) The published protocol is CYCLIC over components until the components' influences on each other reach an equilibrium - a structure this project's coordinate descent over registry FIELDS does not have, because it has no notion of components. (3) The framework's own Table 29 'Validation summaries' row lists 'Transit boardings by transit mode' alongside 'Transit boardings by operator', 'Traffic counts and VMT by volume group', 'Traffic counts and VMT by facility type', 'Traffic counts by screenline' and 'Number of transfers' - so an agent-based agency model DOES plan per-transit-mode validation. It is not reported as a deviation table with bands, which is why the survey's top rung stays empty, but the granularity is standard practice, not unheard of.

calibration_methods.method: EQUILIBRIUM-SEEKING SEARCH between an activity-based demand model and a dynamic traffic assignment (Tallinn) - the only architecture read that measures equilibrium as a DISTANCE BETWEEN CONSECUTIVE ITERATIONS rather than as a score plateau
calibration_methods.family: fixed-point iteration between two coupled models, with a perturbation phase when the iterate stalls
calibration_methods.implemented_in: arXiv 2404.07789, 'An equilibrium-seeking search algorithm for integrating large-scale activity-based and dynamic traffic assignment models', applied to Tallinn (~400,000 inhabitants, >1,100,000 trips per typical day)
calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: the demand/supply iterate itself - not calibration parameters. It is the loop that makes the coupled system settle.
calibration_methods.update_rule: the error measure is the integrated difference in traffic patterns between consecutive iterations, verbatim as rendered: 'Delta_Tf_i = Delta_A_i = |A_i - A_{i-1}| = integral |v_i(mod) - v_{i-1}(mod)| d(mod) for all mod' - i.e. the L1 distance between this iteration's and last iteration's flow pattern, summed over modes.
calibration_methods.objective_evaluations: PUBLISHED: 'Overall, 15 iterations are needed to reach values of the measure of error lower than 10%.' Trajectory read this pass: iterations 1-4 at 0.71, 0.63, 0.60; after a deliberate perturbation, iterations 5-8 fall to 0.34 then 0.14-0.16; the dynamic-assignment phase (9-16) ends at 12% (morning) and 8% (afternoon).
calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: the inter-iteration flow difference falling below 10%; validated afterwards against modal share (private vehicle 49%, PT 25%, walking 24%), morning car-trip totals (~103,000-113,000 legs, 7.9% error) and work/education OD distributions.
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: This is the closest published analogue to the board's own drift test - and it differs in two ways worth taking. (1) It measures the distance between consecutive FLOW PATTERNS, not between consecutive mode-share points; a 0.261 pp drift on twelve shares can hide a flow pattern still moving underneath. (2) It uses a deliberate PERTURBATION when the iterate stalls: the run went 0.71 -> 0.63 -> 0.60 and then only broke to 0.34 after being perturbed. This project's landed arm plateaued and was then FORCED to settle by switching innovation off - the opposite intervention, and the one that produced the +2.211 pp car snap. The published loop perturbs a stalled iterate; ours freezes one.

calibration_methods.method: WHY A CONVERGED MATSim NEED NOT MATCH OBSERVED SHARES - the theory, from MATSim's own book (Floetteroed & Kickhoefer, 'Choice Models in MATSim', ch. 49) and the developers' own thread
calibration_methods.family: not a calibration method - the published account of what MATSim's stationary state IS, and of the biases that decide whether it can reproduce an observation at all
calibration_methods.implemented_in: Chapter 49 of 'The Multi-Agent Transport Simulation MATSim' (Gunnar Floetteroed and Benjamin Kickhoefer), read in full this pass; plus matsim-org/matsim-code-examples issue #25 (Oct 2018), read through the GitHub comments API.
calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: nothing - it explains the object the other methods are calibrating
calibration_methods.update_rule: The chapter's central identity is that an executed plan's probability is a SUM OVER CHOICE SETS: the choice-set-independent probability of selecting plan i factorises into the probability that the concrete choice set C_n arises (which the plan innovation modules draw) and the probability that i is chosen from it (which the plan selection modules draw). The choice set is therefore PART OF the model, not scaffolding around it.
calibration_methods.the_finding: THE SENTENCE THAT DIAGNOSES THIS PROJECT'S LANDED ARM, VERBATIM: 'When a policy study's synthetic choice sets are very different from the alternatives considered in the real world, it is unlikely that the simulation will display correct aggregated quantities or useful sensitivities for policy measures.' And on the measurability of that damage, verbatim: 'MATSim's currently implemented mutation and innovation procedures constitute concrete, yet heuristic, approaches to the choice set generation problem, aiming at valid predictions at the system level. Possible biases induced by these procedures can, however, be difficult to quantify. For example, the current MATSim implementation might, under certain conditions, yield incomplete choice sets and correlated alternatives'.
calibration_methods.the_configuration_finding: AND THE CONFIGURATION THAT THIS PROJECT IS HALF-USING, VERBATIM: a deterministic, plain-MNL-like stationary state needs BOTH settings, not one - 'A fixed choice set C_n is eventually obtained by setting the configuration option fractionOfIterationsToDisableInnovation below one' AND 'Score convergence to its expectation value can be achieved by setting the configuration option fractionOfIterationsToStartScoreMSA below one, meaning that scores will be averaged according to MSA (Method of Successive Averages) for the remaining fraction of iterations.' Disabling innovation WITHOUT score MSA freezes the choice set while leaving the scores to fluctuate with congestion - which is the configuration under which this project's arm snapped +2.211 pp on car at the cutoff and then watched the average plan score fall from 19.2049 to 14.5679.
calibration_methods.objective_evaluations: n/a
calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: The developers' own answer on the executed-vs-best score gap, from matsim-code-examples issue #25: tduberne, 26 Oct 2018 - 'it is quite typical to have the executed score pretty close to the worst score, for those simulation with mode choice enabled'; and, 31 Oct 2018, on whether shares settle - 'Yes, mode shares do stabilize as well, only slower' than scores. So a flat score curve is NOT evidence that shares have settled, and the profession already knows it.
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: It converts the board's open question - why running to convergence made the fit worse - from a mystery into a named, published mechanism with two testable branches. Branch one is CHOICE SET: the board records final pt choice-set coverage at 25.78%, so three quarters of agents never held a pt plan at all, and the chapter says outright that a simulation whose synthetic choice sets differ from the real alternative set is unlikely to display correct aggregated quantities. Branch two is the CUTOFF CONFIGURATION: the book pairs disabling innovation with score MSA, and this project disabled innovation alone. Neither branch is a taste parameter, so neither is reachable by any ASC loop - which is precisely why the board's refusal to tune on this reading is the right call.

calibration_methods.method: AUXILIARY DEMAND - the published reason a resident activity-based model cannot reproduce absolute link volumes, and the acceptance-bar vacuum around it
calibration_methods.family: not a calibration method - a structural completeness requirement on the demand before any count comparison is meaningful
calibration_methods.implemented_in: TF Resource, 'Integrated Travel Demand and Network Models'; and TF Resource, 'Model Validation and Reasonableness Checking / Amount Of Travel'
calibration_methods.what_it_adjusts: the composition of the assigned trip table
calibration_methods.update_rule: VERBATIM: 'Auxiliary demand refers to trips that are not represented in the activity-based model system, such as truck trips, visitor trips, internal-external and external-external trips, and special generator trips.' And: 'in most cases, the auxiliary trip models used in conjunction with activity-based models are similar to those used in conjunction with trip-based models, although additional temporal or spatial detail may be included.'
calibration_methods.the_bar: THE ACCEPTANCE-BAR VACUUM IS WIDER THAN THE LIBRARY RECORDED. The 9 September pass established that TF Resource states 'There are no applicable criteria guidelines for checks of mode choice.' This pass read the Amount-Of-Travel validation page and found the SAME formula applied to the count-side families: 'There are no specific criteria guidelines associated with the trip generation checks described above', and, for external models, truck models and special generators, 'There are no applicable criteria guidelines.' The only two numeric ranges on that page are for trip generation - regionwide productions to attractions 'should fall in the range of 0.90 to 1.10 prior to balancing', and 'a reasonable range is between 1.20 and 1.55 home-based work attractions per employee'. No numeric guideline was found for percent RMSE by volume group, GEH, screenline tolerance, trip-length distribution or average trip length.

calibration_methods.convergence_criterion: n/a
calibration_methods.why_it_matters_here: This is the best structural candidate found for this project's -98.75% MEDIAN at its 30 count stations (mean absolute 91.69%, 7 modelled zeros, best station +35.13%, worst -100.0%, from the landed run's own _fit.json). The published answer is that an activity-based model's RESIDENT trip table is not the thing a count station measures: trucks, visitors, internal-external, external-external and special-generator trips are all outside it by construction and must be supplied separately. This project HAS built two of those - a truck carve and a through-traffic gate seeded from cordon count rows (B.demand registry) - but the deficit's size says the assigned table is still not the population a station counts. IMPORTANT NEGATIVE: no source read this pass attributes a volume deficit of this magnitude to sample scaling; the MUM 2025 downsampling study finds 25% well inside the reliable band. So 'the sample explains it' is NOT supported, and 'auxiliary demand plus station-to-link matching' is where the published literature points instead.
